newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Black still plans Fairfax stake lift.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Black still plans Fairfax stake lift.

text.p: Hollinger International Chairman Conrad Black, who controls 25 percent in Fairfax, said on Wednesday he had repeated to Australian Prime Minister John Howard his desire to increase that stake.
He also said that cash flows generated by Fairfax would be invested back into the company and would be used for some diversification in the future.
"I said to him (Howard) we would look to increase our shareholding," Black told Fairfax's annual meeting.
Black said he had met Howard on Tuesday.
Black said he was respectful of the government's inquiry into current cross media rules and the government's desire to maintain diversity in the industry.
"We believe, however, that a method should be found for liberalising the cross media and foreign ownership rules, while ensuring that no participant has a preponderant influence," he said.
He said also that Hollinger's role in "rescuing" Fairfax from receivership should not be overlooked.
Black said future cash flows would be reinvested into Fairfax.
"We expect the cash flows (from Fairfax) to rise and we expect some of that flow of money to be reinvested sensibly in diversification of our business," Black said.
He had been answering a question about whether Fairfax planned to diversify into communications and other media in the same way that Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd and other company's had.
